label: Born in Mary, Turkmenistan

sources.quote: Valentin Borisovich Aleskovskii was born on June 3th 1912 in the city of Mary (Turkmenistan).

label: Admitted to LTI by Lensovet
Graduated from LTI by Lensovet
Research fellow at Naval Research Institute, Leningrad
Began graduate studies at LTI by Lensovet
Defended candidate thesis 'Active silica'
description: Candidate of chemical sciences degree, roughly equivalent to a Ph.D.; the original idea of the 'framework' hypothesis was outlined the same year.

label: Original idea of 'framework' hypothesis outlined
description: Aleskovskii notes on page 98 of his doctoral dissertation that the original idea was outlined by him in 1940.

label: Senior researcher, Department of Sorption Technology, LTI
Volunteered for the war
description: After returning to the institute he worked as a research assistant in the Department of Physical Chemistry and received government awards for WWII participation.

label: Appointed head of Department of Analytical Chemistry, LTI
Defended doctoral dissertation formulating the 'framework' hypothesis
description: Became Doctor of Chemical Sciences and Professor; the dissertation proposed a new solid state concept of a 'core' surrounded by surface functional groups.

sources.quote: In 1952 he defended his doctoral dissertation (Table 1) and became a Doctor of Chemical Sciences and a Professor.

label: Principles of the molecular layering method created at LTI
description: Aleskovskii and Kol'tsov created and experimentally substantiated the ML principles within LTI by Lensovet.

sources.quote: In the walls of this institute between 1950 and the late 1960s they created and experimentally substantiated the principles of the ML method.

label: Kol'tsov born at Proletarskaya station, Rostov region
Kol'tsov admitted to LTI by Lensovet
Kol'tsov graduated LTI and enrolled as Aleskovskii's graduate student
description: Graduated with a chemical engineering degree and the same year enrolled at the Department of Analytical Chemistry under Aleskovskii.

label: Kol'tsov defended candidate thesis on CCl4 interaction with silica gel
description: Ended the first phase of research under Aleskovskii; the thesis reported molecular layering at atmospheric pressure.

label: Monograph 'Silica Gel: Its Structure and Chemical Properties' published
First full article on the ML method published

sources.quote: The first full article on the ML method appeared in 1965.

label: Kuznetsova defended candidate thesis (IR study of hydrated silica reactions)
description: Advisors were Aleskovskii and IR specialist A. M. Shevyakov; she adopted Kol'tsov's method for HSiCl3, TiCl4 and GeCl4 reactions.

label: Became acting rector of LTI by Lensovet

sources.quote: From 1965 to 1975 V. B. Aleskovskii was acting rector of the LTI by Lensovet.

label: Founded Department of Chemistry of Solids at LTI and became its chair
description: One of the first such departments in the USSR.

label: Volkova defended candidate thesis on chloride reactions with silica gel
Report 'Obtaining materials with desired properties' to USSR Academy of Sciences
description: Given at the General meeting of the branch of physical chemistry and technology of inorganic materials.

label: Kol'tsov defended doctoral dissertation 'Synthesis of solids by the Molecular Layering Method'
description: Final stage of ML method development, laying out its key principles, classification of ML reactions and the term 'chemical assembly'.

sources.quote: The final stage of development of the ML method was S. I. Kol'tsov's doctoral dissertation (Defended on January 20, 1971, Table 1)

label: Attempted to patent ML process; application declined
description: Application 1642785/23-26 'The principles of synthesis of solids' was declined by the patent office.

sources.quote: In 1971, V. B. Aleskovskii and S. I. Kol'tsov attempted to patent the ML process (application № 1642785/23-26, April 07, 1971).

label: Sveshnikova defended candidate thesis on thin oxide layers on silicon
Rachkovskii defended candidate thesis on oxide layers on single-crystal silicon
Elected corresponding member of the USSR Academy of Sciences
Malygin defended candidate thesis on V, Cr, P oxychlorides with silica gel
V. M. Smirnov defended candidate thesis; first mention of 'monolayer effect'
description: Observed a two-orders-of-magnitude increase in catalytic activity of silica gel after one ML monolayer of titanium oxide.

label: Tuz defended candidate thesis on stability of thin oxide layers on silica gel
E. P. Smirnov defended candidate thesis on carbon and TiO2 layers on carbon by ML
Drozd joined ML group as graduate student at Department of Chemistry of Solids
description: A Leningrad Electrotechnical Institute graduate, one of the few physicists in the ML group.

label: Suntola's first ALE patent filed (priority date)
Appointed rector of Leningrad State University

sources.quote: Since 1975, educational, scientific and organizational activities of V. B. Aleskovskii were associated with the Leningrad State University (LSU) since he was appointment as rector of this university.

label: Drozd built first ML system with in situ ellipsometric thickness monitoring
ML dielectric films for MOS structures demonstrated with 'Svetlana'
description: High-k oxides of Cr, Ti, V, Hf, Zr, Ta, Nb and Mo made by ML for MOS structures, in cooperation with the electronics organization Svetlana.

label: Kol'tsov became head of Solid State Chemistry Department at LTI
Monograph 'The stoichiometry and synthesis of solid compounds' published
Organized Department of Solid State Chemistry at LSU
description: Aleskovskii supervised the department until 1986 and then worked there as a professor.

label: Suntola's first atomic layer epitaxy patent published
description: Published in the USSR on February 28, 1981.

label: Article on chemical assembly published in Pravda; Kosygin takes interest
description: Prime Minister Kosygin then ordered a committee from the Academy of Sciences, the Ministry of Education and the State Committee on Science and Technology.

label: Committee rejected proposed Institute of Chemical Assembly of Materials
description: Aleskovskii, Kol'tsov, Malygin and Shevyakov attended; Deputy Minister Kalinin proposed an inter-university program as compromise.

sources.quote: He added that, without the proposed Institute of Chemical Assembly of Materials, the Soviet Union would be forced to purchase ML-based technologies from abroad in the near future.

label: Drozd produced automated vacuum ML setup with analog control
Malkov defended candidate thesis on ML metal oxide layers on carbon fibers
'Chemical assembly of materials' inter-university program founded under Aleskovskii
description: Founded by the Ministry of Higher Education of the RSFSR, led by LSU and LTI by Lensovet; ran 1978–1982.

label: Textbook 'Chemistry of solids' published
Drozd defended candidate thesis on ML oxide coatings on semiconductors
Suntola's second ALE patent (ZnS from ZnCl2/H2S) filed
Pak defended first ML doctoral thesis since Kol'tsov's (quantum-chemical study of oxide coatings)
First experiments on pilot-scale column flow unit for IVS-1 production
description: Conducted by Dergachev under Malygin's supervision.

label: Suntola's second ALE patent published
First Soviet industrial ML products: sorbents FS-1-3 and IVS-1

sources.quote: In the USSR, these were the first industrial products made by the ML method.

label: Ceased supervising LSU Department of Solid State Chemistry; continued as professor
Damyanov defended doctoral thesis on ML catalysts in Bulgaria
Damyanov visited Department of Chemistry of Solids, LTI
Department renamed Chemical Engineering of Materials and Electronics Products
First Soviet ML report at 1st International Symposium on ALE, Espoo/Helsinki
description: Drozd presented the report co-authored with Aleskovskii and handed Suntola an invitation from Aleskovskii to visit LSU.

label: Suntola lectured at LSU Solid State Chemistry Department; met Aleskovskii
description: Aleskovskii told Suntola that his team had developed the ML method, which Suntola called ALE, more than 20 years earlier.

sources.quote: To this, V.B. Aleskovskii answered that he and his team had developed the ML method more than 20 years ago, which Suntola called ALE in his talk.

label: Malygin defended doctoral thesis on ML surface modification of dispersed and porous materials
V. M. Smirnov defended doctoral thesis on surface compounds of silica gel
Monograph 'Chemistry of supramolecular compounds' published
description: Based on lecture notes from his 1990 course 'Course of chemistry of supramolecular compounds'.

label: Last textbook 'Chemical-informational synthesis' published
Russian patent application with Sulimov filed
description: Patent RU 2172731, application 2000119621/04, published 27.08.2001.

label: Kol'tsov died
25th anniversary of LSU Department of Solid State Chemistry
description: Aleskovskii attended; a collection of departmental research articles was published.

label: Malygin asked Aleskovskii why his ideas were not supported in the 1970s
description: At the 2004 conference at SPbSU Aleskovskii replied that his ideas often begin to be understood 20-30 years after they are conceived.

label: Died

sources.quote: S. I. Kol'tsov (passed away May 25, 2003) and V. B. Aleskovskii (passed away January 29, 2006) continued to work in what are among the oldest Russian universities

label: Posthumous article on quantum chemical technologies published
CNEEM department celebrated 40th anniversary with collected papers
Department renamed Chemical Nanotechnology and Electronics Engineering Materials (CNEEM)
Virtual Project on the History of ALD initiated
VPHA conclusions on early ML/ALD history presented at Baltic ALD, Helsinki
'On the Early History of ALD: Molecular Layering' presented at AVS ALD, Kyoto
